events.summary: The live activation message declared a baton SHA-256 that did not match the exact committed Git blob.

The committed baton, baton-integrity record, content seal, owner manifest, and final-delta manifest independently agreed on the exact Git-blob digest; the live mismatch remains retained at zero credit and Vesper history was not rewritten.
A naive x2 manifest replay treated twenty CRLF-projected YAML checkout-byte counts as canonical mismatches.

The predecessor contract and retained Vesper failure were reread; all 208 normalized-LF Git-blob SHA-256 values matched, while the legacy checkout-byte metadata differences retain zero conversion credit.
The first target-lane uniqueness wrapper contained an invalid nested PowerShell expression and stopped at parse time before running Git.
A simple scalar uniqueness probe established that the Lyren target lane and branch were absent and changed no repository state.
The second combined target-lane probe exited without attributable scalar output and earned zero setup credit.
A bounded line-oriented probe established target absence, branch absence, exact source head, clean source state, and sufficient D-drive capacity.
The first broad x1 patch failed its exact-context verification because one predecessor-phase label had already changed during namespace adaptation.
Narrow exact-context patches and dynamically bounded marker replacements updated only the untracked Lyren x1 scaffolding.
The first manifest-contract search named a nonexistent build-prefixed x2 manifest script and returned a path error.
A bounded filename listing identified the exact family-current manifest script, whose code and retained CRLF failure contract were then read completely.
The first recursive cleanup request for newly generated Python bytecode was rejected by command safety before execution.
No repository byte changed; bytecode remained ignored and all later Python invocations disable bytecode writes.
A second nonrecursive bytecode cleanup request was also rejected by command safety before execution.
Cleanup retries stopped; Git status, owner manifests, and materialization accounting exclude the ignored generated cache.

The first source-bounded semantic audit rejected one exact historical title and ten additional titles at or above the preregistered 0.75 token-Jaccard ceiling, then stopped before writing x1 documents.
Only the eleven cited Lyren titles were rewritten with narrower audiovisual-catalogue semantics; every unflagged proposal and the immutable source remained unchanged before the isolated audit retry.
The first eleven-title patch failed exact-context verification on the final trailing-comma line and changed no file.
A narrower exact-context patch changed only the eleven quarantined Lyren titles before the isolated audit retry.
The second source-bounded audit cleared ten rewritten collisions but retained the terminal-gate title exactly at the 0.75 quarantine threshold.
Only that terminal-gate title was rewritten as a distinct readiness denylist before one further isolated audit retry.
The third audit exposed an unintended sixty-first title, which shifted the rights gate into proposal 060 and left it exactly at the 0.75 quarantine threshold.
The extra planning-only practice-boundary row was removed, restoring exactly sixty titles with rows 055 through 057 open and rows 058 through 060 exact-gated.
The fourth audit confirmed the sixty-row partition but retained the audiovisual rights and taonga authority gate exactly at the 0.75 semantic threshold.
Only proposal 059 was rewritten as an unpopulated broadcast-description authority reservation before the next isolated audit retry.
The first bounded owner-code scan found a duplicate Lyren family anchor plus inherited microfilm labels in the untracked x2 scaffolding.
Only Lyren-owned untracked scaffolding was corrected to the immutable Vesper source, frozen Lyren x1, audiovisual domain, current roster, and protected route before builder or test execution.
The first direct import-based x2 constant probe omitted the derived repository scripts directory and failed with ModuleNotFoundError before execution.
The isolated read-only probe inserted the exact owner scripts directory into sys.path and then verified anchors, baseline, and roster without changing repository bytes.
The first x2 owner suite retained zero success credit after 19 passes and two failures exposed stale template expectations for operational-pair and Method Flow counts.
Only the count expectations were updated to include every truthful Lyren failure/recovery pair and its derived Method Flow totals before the isolated x2 suite retry.
